29 Which diagram shows the pattern of the electric field between a positively charged metal sphere
and a negatively charged metal plate?
A
B
+

–

hints: Notice the charges: the top sphere is marked + and the bottom plate is marked -. Recall which charge field lines start on and which they end on.
Connect this to the conductor rule: electric field lines must meet a metal surface at 90 degrees, leaving the sphere radially and entering the flat plate vertically.
Now compare straight versus curved outer lines and check the arrow direction on each diagram to find the pattern that satisfies both the direction and the right-angle rule.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: a small + sphere above a large flat - plate. By definition electric field direction is the force on a positive test charge, so lines must start on + and end on -.
Apply the conductor boundary rule: lines leave the spherical surface along radii, so normal to the sphere, and arrive at the flat plate normal to the plate, so vertical at the plate.

This means the central line is straight down, while outer lines must curve outward to still meet both surfaces at right angles. Straight diagonal lines cannot be normal to the sphere over its lower half.
Check arrows: they must point downward from sphere to plate. Only the diagram with downward arrows and curved outer lines that are normal to both surfaces satisfies both rules. This is option B.

A.explanation: Direction from + sphere to - plate is correct, but straight lines meeting the sphere at an angle are wrong because field lines must leave a conductor surface at right angles.

B.explanation: Lines go from positive to negative, leave the sphere radially and meet the negative plate at right angles, with correct curved shape.

C.explanation: Arrows point from the negative plate toward the positive sphere, which is opposite to the defined direction of electric field from positive to negative.

D.explanation: The curved shape meeting surfaces at right angles is correct, but the arrows point upward from negative to positive, which reverses the field direction.
